correctness.rationale: For distinct a,b, ba is absent precisely when last(a)<first(b); missing aa identifies letters occurring once. This recovers exactly the pair (P,S) from the signature. Singleton positions are disjoint; every neighboring interval of a singleton contains its point, so marked vertices are independent and simplicial. Conversely enlarge intervals by less than half the minimum comparable gap (if there are no comparisons, any sufficiently small positive enlargement works). This makes all incomparabilities strict overlaps while retaining every comparison; a further small perturbation removes endpoint ties. For a simplicial marked vertex its closed neighborhood is a pairwise strictly intersecting finite interval family, so max of left endpoints is strictly below min of right endpoints. Choose an interior point avoiding all endpoints and contract the marked interval there. Independence means the contracted intervals were disjoint, so the contractions do not interfere. The endpoint word realizes the original pair (P,S), uses one occurrence per marked letter and two per unmarked letter, and meets the unavoidable lower bound. Adjacent simplicial vertices have identical closed neighborhoods: each neighbor of one must be adjacent to the other or equal to it. Hence the induced components are cliques and each contributes the choice of zero or one marked letter. This yields the stated labeled polynomial, including isolated vertices and q=1, when it is z+z^2.
residual_risks: The archived exhaustive small-alphabet histogram comparison through q=5 is finite corroboration, not the arbitrary-q proof. Full support, labeled letters and scattered depth two are essential to the stated interpretation.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Even a shortest-word procedure for each signature does not characterize which abstract pair orders and repetition flags are realizable. The new condition requires both independence and simpliciality and a simultaneous Helly realization, which in turn yields the clique-product enumerator.

evidence: The piecewise-complexity paper uses reduced words and the minimality index, measuring the least subsequence depth at which a word is reduced. Indexed binary two-marker classes use clipped gap coordinates under fixed content.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The depth needed to detect minimality is not the shortest-length distribution at fixed depth. The fixed-content binary object does not encode independent simplicial markings for arbitrary labeled alphabets.

value.rationale: It answers a natural inverse question: which distinct-letter ordering patterns can coexist with specified singleton letters? The exact marking criterion makes this decision from the incomparability graph and gives an all-alphabet length enumerator, qualitatively more than reproducing an index table.
residual_risks: The sum still runs over labeled interval orders; no fast enumeration algorithm or higher-depth extension is established.
